title: Lackman and Carson carnival, Ida Cox and Blind Denslow
summary: They confirm the carnival name, discuss Ida Cox on minstrel shows, and Lee recalls the blind dancer Denslow.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Oh, the carnival that you traveled with was Lightman and ...
Lackman. When I played the tape back, I wasn't sure what the word was. What was it?
Okay, that was a word I wasn't sure of.
And you mentioned Ida Cox, and I found in looking her up, that she toured with White and Clark's minstrels.
Well, see, I remember her as minstrel -- I remember her with minstrel shows, and I don't remember ...

No, you never do. But see, when you're that young, somehow you catalog these things and you do remember them, you know. And I don't know if I told you about -- there was a team -- someone would remember -- on one of the minstrel shows we were on, the man's name was Blind Denslow, and now I never thought I would ever remember his name again, but just in talking to you -- he was a blind man that performed on stage, you know, and he used to break the show up. And his wife would have to lead him to the wings, you know, and he'd go out on stage, and he was a singer and a dancer, and then, you know, she would call and he would go back in to the wings.
That's pretty unusual. I've never heard of a blind dancer.
No, I haven't heard of any others, but he did, because I remember his name was Denslow -- it's an
odd name, but he was on that minstrel show, the one that I said that we were on around Baltimore, when I saw those steps and things.
